title: Type system (language view)
intro: C# checks types before your program runs. Every variable has a fixed type — either written by you or inferred with `var`. This module teaches which built-in types to pick, how value and reference types copy or alias, how null and defaults work, and how to convert and test types safely.

conceptCards.title: var is type inference
conceptCards.summary: `var` asks the compiler to pick the type from the initializer. It is not JavaScript `var` and not `dynamic`.

conceptCards.title: decimal for money and grades
conceptCards.summary: Use `decimal` (with `m` suffix) for currency and GPA. Use `double` for graphics and science math.

conceptCards.title: Copy vs alias
conceptCards.summary: Value types copy on assignment. Reference types alias the same object. Boxing wraps a value as `object`.
conceptCards.example: `list2 = list1` — both see the same list.

conceptCards.title: Locals must be assigned
conceptCards.summary: Fields default to zero or null. Locals must be assigned on every path before read — or the build fails.

conceptCards.title: int? for missing numbers
conceptCards.summary: `int?` is `Nullable<int>` — a struct that can report "no value." Different from `string?` (module 07).

conceptCards.title: is, as, typeof, GetType
conceptCards.summary: `typeof` is compile-time. `GetType()` is run-time. `is` tests compatibility; `as` returns null on failure.

conceptCards.title: class, struct, record, enum
conceptCards.summary: Pick class for identity, struct for small copyable data, record for value equality, enum for fixed constants.

conceptCards.title: object root and dynamic
conceptCards.summary: Every type derives from `object` via the Common Type System (CTS). `dynamic` defers member lookup to run time.
